Ming-3.0-audio-flash

Hear clearly. Understand deeply. Act intelligently.

Ming-3.0-audio-flash is a native audio-language model from inclusionAI. It accepts audio together with text instructions and supports speech recognition, spoken question answering, audio understanding, audio reasoning, and optional synthesized-speech responses.
GitHub · 🤖 ModelScope · 🤗 Flash · 🤗 Tiny · 💻 Examples
## Model Summary | Property | Description | | --- | --- | | Developer | inclusionAI | | Model type | Native audio-language Mixture-of-Experts model | | Parameters | 126B total parameters, 6.5B activated per inference step | | Inputs | Audio and text instructions | | Outputs | Text, or text with optional synthesized speech | | Primary languages | Chinese and English, including varied accents and dialects | | License | MIT | ## Highlights - **Complex speech recognition:** Handles Chinese and English speech, dialects, accents, noisy environments, and multi-speaker recordings. - **Long-audio understanding:** Comprehends and analyzes long-form recordings. - **Multidimensional perception:** Understands speech, non-speech sounds, acoustic scenes, and music. - **Audio reasoning:** Answers questions and performs reasoning over audio content. - **Audio interaction:** Produces text responses and can optionally synthesize speech with built-in voices or a reference voice. ## Architecture Ming-3.0-audio-flash combines an audio encoder and projector with a Mixture-of-Experts language backbone. An optional Talker generates speech responses from the model's output.

## Quick Start with Transformers The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the repository code before enabling `trust_remote_code=True`. ```bash git clone https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash.git cd Ming-3.0-audio-flash python -m venv .venv-transformers source .venv-transformers/bin/activate pip install -r requirements-transformers.txt ``` ### Audio Understanding ```bash python examples/transformers_audio.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --prompt "Please answer the question in the audio." ``` ### Speech Recognition ```bash python examples/transformers_audio.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --task asr \ --max-new-tokens 256 \ --no-repeat-ngram-size 10 ``` The validated ASR prompt asks the model to identify the spoken language and place a tab between the language label and transcription. ### Direct Python Usage ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash" audio_path = "examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, use_fast=False, ) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True, ).eval() messages = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio", "audio": audio_path}, {"type": "text", "text": "Please answer the question in the audio."}, ], } ] inputs = processor(messages).to(model.device) inputs["audio_feats"] = inputs["audio_feats"].to(model.dtype) with torch.inference_mode(): output_ids = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False, ) generated_ids = output_ids[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :] response = processor.decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens=True).strip() print(response) ``` ## Speech Output The Talker example supports built-in voices and reference-audio voice prompting: ```bash python examples/transformers_thinker_talker.py \ --model inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --audio examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --voice US_Stella \ --output output.wav ``` See the [voice guide](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/docs/voices.md) for available voice names and reference-audio usage. ## Serving ### vLLM-Omni ```bash export MODEL_PATH=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash MING_OUTPUT_MODE=text ./scripts/serve_vllm_omni.sh "$MODEL_PATH" ``` The reference 128K serving profile uses tensor parallelism across four 80 GB H800 GPUs. Select the deployment YAML that matches text-only or Talker output. On particularly long audio inputs, the four-GPU profiles may OOM; in that case, switch to the corresponding eight-GPU fallback profile (`deploy/*_8gpu.yaml`), which sets `tensor_parallel_size: 8` across GPUs 0–7 (and the Talker reuses GPU 7). See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/README.md#vllm-omni) for details. For speech output, start the audio profile and select an IP or registered voice with the vLLM-Omni client's `--voice` option: ```bash MING_OUTPUT_MODE=audio ./scripts/serve_vllm_omni.sh "$MODEL_PATH" python examples/vllm_omni_audio_chat.py examples/audio/introduce_ant_group.wav \ --audio-response \ --voice US_Stella \ --output-audio outputs/answer.wav ``` The client sends this selection as Chat Completions `audio.voice: {"id": "..."}`. vLLM-Omni uses the built-in IP voice `灵小柔` when no voice is specified. The model directory also provides `灵楷` and `US_James` as preset reference voices under `voice_presets/voice_audio/`, with their matching transcripts in `voice_presets/voice_prompts.json`. Both names are also available as built-in IP voices. ### SGLang ```bash export MODEL_PATH=inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash ./scripts/serve_sglang.sh "$MODEL_PATH" ``` The validated SGLang profile uses four GPUs and provides text output. See the [SGLang example](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash/blob/main/examples/sglang_audio_chat.py) for client usage. ### SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/) serves transcription, audio chat, and speech synthesis from one server. Serving uses two GPUs: `--thinker.tp_size 2` places the thinker on both visible devices, the audio encoder uses GPU 0, and speech synthesis uses GPU 1. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 sgl-omni serve \ --model-path inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-audio-flash \ --thinker.tp_size 2 ``` The server exposes OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/speech`, and `/v1/chat/completions` endpoints. See the [SGLang-Omni cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming3_audio.html) for client examples, including voice cloning with `ref_audio` and `ref_text`. ## Evaluation ### Speech Recognition

# UniFlow-Audio GGUF

GGUF packs for [uniflow.cpp](https://github.com/audiohacking/uniflow.cpp) —
C++17 GGML inference for [UniFlow-Audio](https://github.com/wsntxxn/UniFlow-Audio)
(text-to-audio / text-to-music). No Python at runtime.

**Small / Base / Large** = DiT capacity.  
**F16 / Q8_0 / Q4_0** on `dit-*.gguf` = DiT weight encoding.  
**T5 is per pack** (not one shared F32 blob): small uses **Q4_0**, base and large use **Q8_0**.
F16 T5 is not published (unsupported on the CPU encoder path).

**Recommended default: Base + `dit-Q8_0.gguf`.**

## Packs

| Directory | Upstream | T5 | DiT files |
|-----------|----------|----|-----------|
| `uniflow-audio-v1.1-small/` | [Small](https://huggingface.co/wsntxxn/UniFlow-Audio-v1.1-Small) | Q4_0 (~183 MB) | F16 / Q8_0 / Q4_0 |
| `uniflow-audio-v1.1-base/` | [Base](https://huggingface.co/wsntxxn/UniFlow-Audio-v1.1-Base) | Q8_0 (~346 MB) | F16 / Q8_0 / Q4_0 |
| `uniflow-audio-v1.1-large/` | [Large](https://huggingface.co/wsntxxn/UniFlow-Audio-v1.1-Large) | Q8_0 (~346 MB) | F16 / Q8_0 / Q4_0 |

Also in every pack: `vae.gguf`, `instructions.gguf`, `spiece.model` (~93 MB).

## Quick start

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/audiohacking/uniflow.cpp
cd uniflow.cpp
make metal

# requires: pip install -U "huggingface_hub[cli]"
./scripts/download_gguf.sh                 # base + dit-Q8_0 (+ T5 Q8_0)

./build-metal/uniflow-audio --model base --quant Q8_0 \
  --caption "a man is speaking while a dog barks" \
  --output output/out.wav \
  --duration 5 --steps 25 --cfg 5.0 --sway -1 --seed 42
```

Defaults match the UniFlow Space T2A demo: CFG **5.0**, steps **25**, sway **-1**, **24 kHz**.

See the [uniflow.cpp README](https://github.com/audiohacking/uniflow.cpp#readme) for full CLI options.

## License

Upstream UniFlow-Audio is MIT. Follow Flan-T5 terms for `t5_encoder.gguf` /
`spiece.model`. Conversion scripts live in uniflow.cpp `convert/`.

![Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe overview: one speech LLM transcribes a recording in the style selected by the instruction](hero.png) **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, offline speech and audio model** for transcription in 40 languages, with support for recordings up to one hour and a 65,536-token context. Its hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture activates approximately **4.3B parameters**, including the audio encoder, and it is released in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 precision. [Get started ↓](#quick-start) · [Explore the tasks ↓](#prompt-guide) · [See the evidence ↓](#results-at-a-glance) · [NeMo Speech ↗](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech)
Table of contents - [Model Summary](#model-summary) - [Results at a Glance](#results-at-a-glance) - [Efficiency](#efficiency) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Prompt Guide](#prompt-guide) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [Language Support Matrix](#language-support-matrix) - [Training, Testing, and Evaluation Datasets](#training-testing-and-evaluation-datasets) - [Benchmark Results](#benchmark-results) - [Inference Setup and Prompts](#inference-setup-and-prompts) - [Ethical Considerations](#ethical-considerations)

# Model Overview ### Description NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe is an offline speech and audio model that processes recordings, together with text instructions and optional context, into text responses. NVIDIA developed this [Speech-Augmented Language Model (SALM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09424) for multilingual transcription, speech translation, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, timestamp prediction, language identification, and audio question answering. The training mixture also includes a small amount of text instruction following and PII tagging/redaction tasks. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ### Model Summary | | | |:---|:---| | **Total Parameters** | 34B (4.3B active), including the audio encoder | | **Architecture** | Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts language model with a Parallel Expert Encoder (Transformer ASR encoder and speaker encoder) | | **Precision** | BF16 (full-precision reference weights); [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) variants are available | | **Context Length** | 65,536 tokens; recordings up to 1 hour | | **Inputs / Outputs** | Audio and text / text, with optional word timestamps | | **Languages** | 40; see the [language support matrix](#language-support-matrix) | | **Tasks** | Transcription in verbatim or written form, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, speech translation, language identification, and audio question answering | | **Deployment** | 1× H100 80 GB; see the [hardware compatibility table](#software-integration) | | **Speculative Decoding** | Native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP); optional DFlash2 draft model | | **Reasoning Mode** | Configurable through the chat template (`enable_thinking=True/False`) | | **Recommended Sampling** | Transcription, translation, and language identification: temperature 0, reasoning off; audio understanding: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, reasoning on | | **Best For** | Highest accuracy, customization, and fine-tuning | | **License** | [OpenMDW-1.1](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/) | ### Results at a Glance Results captured on October 12, 2026. Error rates are percentages. **↓ Lower is better.** Complete results are listed under [Benchmark Results](#benchmark-results). **Best published results** | Capability | Benchmark | Metric | Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe | Next best published | |:---|:---|:---|:---|:---| | Multi-speaker ASR | AMI, CALLHOME, Mixer 6, NOTSOFAR-1 full sessions | Mean cpWER ↓ | **15.80** | DiCoW v3.3 + DiariZen 16.83 | | Style control | Preference-ASR | WER ↓, default / instructed | **7.56 / 6.16** | Canary-Qwen 8.16 / 8.36 | **Best open-weight results** | Capability | Benchmark | Metric | Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe | Next best open-weight model | |:---|:---|:---|:---|:---| | English ASR | Open ASR Leaderboard, 9 public sets | Mean WER ↓ | **4.71** | Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 4.94 | | Long-form ASR | Open ASR Leaderboard, long-form | Mean WER ↓ | **10.98** | Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 13.37 | | Multilingual ASR | Multilingual Open ASR Leaderboard, 7 languages | Mean WER ↓ | **4.62** | Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 6.49 | ### Efficiency ![Throughput versus median request latency of the Nemotron Transcribe NIM on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU for BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 with and without speculative decoding](serving_performance.png) With the optimized vLLM implementation in the Nemotron Transcribe NIM, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU transcribes up to 2,238 seconds of audio per second (NVFP4 with DFlash2 speculative decoding) and returns the transcript of a 30-second recording in 0.13 seconds. These serving optimizations are not yet part of the open-source release; we aim to upstream them to NeMo Speech and vLLM at a later date. Install both and download the checkpoint as described in [Environment Setup](#environment-setup). ```bash export VLLM_PLUGINS=nemo_speechlm export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=3600 export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=180 # Word timestamps require the V1 model runner. export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 vllm serve ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --served-model-name nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \ --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 192 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-async-scheduling \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":{"count":6,"length":120000000}}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}' \ --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 \ --trust-request-mm-kwargs \ --middleware nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm.ctc_serving.ctc_timestamp_middleware ``` Once the server has loaded the model, transcribe a recording: ```python import base64 from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") audio = base64.b64encode(open("audio.wav", "rb").read()).decode() response = client.chat.completions.create( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "Transcribe the following audio."}, {"type": "audio_url", "audio_url": {"url": f"data:audio/wav;base64,{audio}"}}, ]}], temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}, "skip_special_tokens": False}, ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` See [Inference Setup and Prompts](#inference-setup-and-prompts) for other configurations, reasoning, word timestamps, and task-specific prompts. use `--host` and `--port` to change this. The settings target an H100 with 80 GB of GPU memory; other hardware or workloads may need a different `--gpu-memory-utilization`, `--max-model-len`, or `--max-num-seqs`. The `--middleware` and `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` options let requests opt into [word timestamps](#word-timestamps-and-speaker-diarization). To change the configuration, modify the command as follows: | Configuration | Change | | --- | --- | | Eight GPUs: one data-parallel engine per GPU, with expert parallelism (TP=1, DP=8, EP=8) | Add `--data-parallel-size 8 --api-server-count 8 --enable-expert-parallel --disable-custom-all-reduce` | | MTP with two proposed tokens (MTP2) | Set `"num_speculative_tokens":2` | | No speculative decoding | Remove `--speculative-config` | #### Speculative Decoding Speculative decoding proposes several tokens at once and verifies them with the main model. The checkpoint contains two MTP depths implemented with a repeated layer. MTP8 reuses that layer to propose eight tokens; it does not require eight distinct trained MTP layers. The best mode depends on the GPU and the workload. Approximate throughput for batched English ASR on **one NVIDIA H100 80 GB**, using tuned serving settings: | Decoding mode | Approximate BF16 RTFx | | --- | ---: | | MTP off | Not measured | | MTP2 | 410 | | MTP8 | 270 | | DFlash2 K=7 | 340 | | DFlash2 K=15 | 260 | RTFx is total audio duration divided by processing time: 340 RTFx means about 340 seconds of audio processed per second under batch load. These are rough throughput estimates, excluding server startup, for the English Open ASR and Monsoon datasets with reasoning disabled. Throughput depends on recording length, output length, batch size, and GPU memory settings; it is not a single-request latency estimate. Keep ReplaySSM (`--use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none`) and prefix caching disabled, as in the command above. The first requests after startup are slower while kernels are compiled and warmed up.

#### Send a Request Send audio to the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with an OpenAI-compatible client. The following function covers transcription, reasoning, and word timestamps: ```python import base64 from pathlib import Path from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") def ask(audio_path, prompt, system_prompt="", reasoning=False, timestamps=False): audio = base64.b64encode(Path(audio_path).read_bytes()).decode() messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}] if system_prompt else [] messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio_url", "audio_url": {"url": f"data:audio/wav;base64,{audio}"}}, ]}) extra_body = { "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": reasoning}, "skip_special_tokens": False, # keep speaker and event tags "spaces_between_special_tokens": False, "seed": 0, } if reasoning: extra_body.update(top_k=-1, thinking_token_budget=17408) extra_body["chat_template_kwargs"]["reasoning_budget"] = 16384 if timestamps: extra_body["mm_processor_kwargs"] = {"capture_ctc_timestamps": True} return client.chat.completions.create( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B", messages=messages, temperature=0.6 if reasoning else 0, top_p=0.95 if reasoning else 1.0, max_tokens=20480 if reasoning else 16384, extra_body=extra_body, ) response = ask("audio.wav", "Transcribe the following audio.") print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` A dense one-hour conversation can need about 20,000 output tokens. For long recordings, raise `max_tokens` or remove it, so that the transcript is not truncated. Transcription uses temperature 0 with reasoning disabled. For audio understanding, enable reasoning and ask a question about the audio: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", "What is happening in this audio?", reasoning=True) ``` This sets temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k disabled, seed 0, a 20,480-token completion limit, and a 16,384-token reasoning budget with a 1,024-token allowance to finish reasoning. Use the task instructions documented under [Evaluation Prompts](#evaluation-prompts) as `prompt` and `system_prompt`. #### Word Timestamps and Speaker Diarization The checkpoint bundles the CTC heads used to align the generated transcript to the audio. With `--middleware` set as in the server command above, request timestamps with `timestamps=True`, together with a speaker-tagged transcription prompt: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. " "Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. " "Write numbers in their standard written form. " "Put speaker tags on the transcription." ), timestamps=True) alignment = response.model_dump()["ctc_timestamps"] if alignment["error"] is not None: raise RuntimeError(alignment["error"]) for word in alignment["words"]: print(word["word"], word["start"], word["end"], word["speaker"]) ``` The response contains a top-level `ctc_timestamps` object: - `words`: word text, start and end times in seconds relative to the input audio, and the transcript's speaker tag. - `diarization`: speaker activity segments derived from the audio. - `speaker_tag_to_diarization_speaker`: the mapping between transcript tags and diarization speakers. - `error`: `null` on success, or an alignment failure reason. Check this field before using the timestamps. Timestamp requests accept one audio recording, `stream=false`, and `n=1`. Keep `skip_special_tokens=false` and ask for speaker tags when speaker attribution is needed. A transcript without speaker tags is aligned as a single speaker. Use the `diarization` segments, rather than word timestamps, when evaluating diarization. ### SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni) serves this model for whole-file transcription on `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, on one GPU, from the BF16 or FP8 checkpoint (both validated on one H100 80 GB and one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) prompt = [None, speaker_attributed_prompt] inputs = processor.apply_transcription_request(audio, prompt=prompt).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024) texts = processor.decode(outputs[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) print([text.replace(processor.tokenizer.pad_token, "") for text in texts]) ```

Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) conversation = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio", "path": samples + "diarization_example.mp3"}, ], } ] inputs = processor.apply_chat_template( conversation, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=True, enable_thinking=False, ).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024) text = processor.decode(outputs[0, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) print(text) ``` `processor.extract_speaker_dict` splits the output into one dictionary per speaker turn: ```python for turn in processor.extract_speaker_dict(text): print(turn) ```

![Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe overview: one speech LLM transcribes a recording in the style selected by the instruction](hero.png) **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, offline speech and audio model** for transcription in 40 languages, with support for recordings up to one hour and a 65,536-token context. All benchmark results reported in this model card were computed for the BF16 model. Averaged over the transcription benchmarks, its error rate is **3.6% higher** in relative terms than that of the BF16 model. # Model Overview ### Description NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe is an offline speech and audio model that processes recordings, together with text instructions and optional context, into text responses. NVIDIA developed this [Speech-Augmented Language Model (SALM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09424) for multilingual transcription, speech translation, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, timestamp prediction, language identification, and audio question answering. The training mixture also includes a small amount of text instruction following and PII tagging/redaction tasks. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ### Model Summary | | | |:---|:---| | **Total Parameters** | 34B (4.3B active), including the audio encoder | | **Architecture** | Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts language model with a Parallel Expert Encoder (Transformer ASR encoder and speaker encoder) | | **Precision** | NVFP4 decoder with FP8 layers (ModelOpt post-training quantization of the [BF16 model](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B)) | | **Context Length** | 65,536 tokens; recordings up to 1 hour | | **Inputs / Outputs** | Audio and text / text, with optional word timestamps | | **Languages** | 40; see the [language support matrix](#language-support-matrix) | | **Tasks** | Transcription in verbatim or written form, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, speech translation, language identification, and audio question answering | | **Deployment** | 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB); Blackwell GPUs only; see the [hardware compatibility table](#software-integration) | | **Speculative Decoding** | Native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP); optional DFlash2 draft model | | **Reasoning Mode** | Configurable through the chat template (`enable_thinking=True/False`) | | **Recommended Sampling** | Transcription, translation, and language identification: temperature 0, reasoning off; audio understanding: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, reasoning on | | **Best For** | Lowest memory use and highest throughput on Blackwell GPUs | | **License** | [OpenMDW-1.1](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/) | ### Results at a Glance Results captured on October 12, 2026. See [hardware, runtime, and operating system compatibility](#software-integration). #### Quantized Runtime and Environment This is a ModelOpt mixed-precision export, with NVFP4 decoder layers, FP8 Mamba layers, FP8 audio encoder, and FP8 MTP head. **It requires a Blackwell GPU.** The export declares no KV-cache scheme, so set `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` explicitly; `auto` would not select the FP8 KV cache used in validation. `--dtype bfloat16` selects the compute and residual dtype; it does not convert the quantized checkpoint back to BF16. Let vLLM detect the ModelOpt quantization from `config.json`, and do not override it with a different quantization method. Inference requires **vLLM 0.32.0** and the latest NeMo Speech main branch, which provides the vLLM plugin for this model. NeMo Speech main supports the ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` scheme and resolves the per-layer FP8 map of the audio encoder. Confirm that startup reports `quantization=modelopt_mixed` and 128 FP8 audio-encoder linear layers. Install both into one environment with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and download the checkpoint: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech.git nemo-speech cd nemo-speech uv venv --python 3.13 .venv UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$PWD/.venv uv sync --extra asr --extra vllm --locked --no-install-project uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e . # PyAV decodes compressed audio formats, such as M4A, without a system FFmpeg. uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps av==19.0.2 # vLLM requires OpenCV, which NeMo's dependency settings exclude. uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93 source .venv/bin/activate hf download nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4 --local-dir ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4 ``` FlashInfer compiles the quantized attention kernels on first use, which requires `nvcc` from a CUDA 13 toolkit on `PATH`, for example `export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH`. The first startup therefore takes several minutes; see [Kernel Cache and Measurement Warmup](#kernel-cache-and-measurement-warmup) to reuse the compiled kernels. #### Start the Server The following single-GPU profile was tested on **one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB)**, with MTP speculative decoding proposing eight tokens (MTP8): ```bash export VLLM_PLUGINS=nemo_speechlm # Allow vLLM to decode recordings up to one hour long (the default is 600 seconds). export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=3600 export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=180 # Word timestamps require the V1 model runner. export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 # Keep the optimized CUTLASS FP8 kernels validated on RTX PRO 6000. export VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel vllm serve ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4 \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-async-scheduling \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":{"count":1,"length":57600000}}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}' \ --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 \ --trust-request-mm-kwargs \ --middleware nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm.ctc_serving.ctc_timestamp_middleware ``` The server listens on `127.0.0.1:8000`; use `--host` and `--port` to change this. Client concurrency is separate from the 64-sequence engine limit. This profile admits one recording of up to one hour per request (`length` is in samples at 16 kHz). Validate memory headroom for long recordings under the intended load. The `--middleware` and `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` options let requests opt into [word timestamps](#word-timestamps-and-speaker-diarization). To disable speculative decoding, remove `--speculative-config`. Keep ReplaySSM (`--use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none`) and prefix caching disabled, as in the command above. The first requests after startup are slower while kernels are compiled and warmed up. Keep the optimized FP8 and NVFP4 kernels rather than substituting unquantized or generic PyTorch implementations.

DFlash2 and MTP are alternatives and are not combined. vLLM 0.32.0 needs a small fix to its DFlash2 implementation; without it, the server can fail when requests finish. Apply it once to the environment: ```bash python - <<'EOF_PATCH' from pathlib import Path import vllm path = Path(vllm.__file__).parent / "model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash2.py" source = path.read_text() if "safe_anchor_token_ids" not in source: old = " successors = successor_table[candidate_ids]\n" anchor = " anchor_token_ids[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, top_k)," assert source.count(old) == 1 and source.count(anchor) == 1, "unexpected vLLM version" source = source.replace(old, ( " safe_anchor_token_ids = anchor_token_ids.clamp(\n" " min=0, max=predecessor_table.shape[0] - 1\n" " )\n" + old )).replace(anchor, " safe_anchor_token_ids[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, top_k),") path.write_text(source) EOF_PATCH ``` The fix modifies vLLM source code (Copyright contributors to the vLLM project), which is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, not under OpenMDW-1.1; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Then start the server with the following options instead of `--speculative-config` and `--middleware` from the command above. Word timestamps are not available with DFlash2, so the CTC alignment is disabled: ```bash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":15,"model":"nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2"}' \ --hf-overrides '{"ctc_timestamps":{"enabled":false}}' ``` vLLM runs DFlash2 only on its V2 model runner, so also run `unset VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` before starting the server.
#### Kernel Cache and Measurement Warmup FlashInfer's JIT cache uses `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE/.cache/flashinfer`; `XDG_CACHE_HOME` alone does not control it. To avoid recompiling kernels after a restart, set `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` to a persistent directory, for example a bind-mounted directory in a container. Keep generated caches separate for different runtime versions and GPU architectures. Before measuring DFlash15 latency or throughput, prebuild the required FlashInfer XQA kernels with `gen_xqa_module(...).build_and_load()` and warm up each input length and concurrency level. Exclude initialization, compilation, and warmup from steady-state timing, and report cold-start time separately. Check that no kernels are compiled during the measurement and that there are no request errors or out-of-memory failures; report responses that reach the token limit and KV-cache preemptions. Set request token limits to fit the task and the available context. #### Send a Request Send audio to the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with an OpenAI-compatible client. The following function covers transcription, reasoning, and word timestamps: ```python import base64 from pathlib import Path from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") def ask(audio_path, prompt, system_prompt="", reasoning=False, timestamps=False): audio = base64.b64encode(Path(audio_path).read_bytes()).decode() messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}] if system_prompt else [] messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio_url", "audio_url": {"url": f"data:audio/wav;base64,{audio}"}}, ]}) extra_body = { "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": reasoning}, "skip_special_tokens": False, # keep speaker and event tags "spaces_between_special_tokens": False, "seed": 0, } if reasoning: extra_body.update(top_k=-1, thinking_token_budget=17408) extra_body["chat_template_kwargs"]["reasoning_budget"] = 16384 if timestamps: extra_body["mm_processor_kwargs"] = {"capture_ctc_timestamps": True} return client.chat.completions.create( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4", messages=messages, temperature=0.6 if reasoning else 0, top_p=0.95 if reasoning else 1.0, max_tokens=20480 if reasoning else 16384, extra_body=extra_body, ) response = ask("audio.wav", "Transcribe the following audio.") print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` A dense one-hour conversation can need about 20,000 output tokens. For long recordings, raise `max_tokens` or remove it, so that the transcript is not truncated. Transcription uses temperature 0 with reasoning disabled. For audio understanding, enable reasoning and ask a question about the audio: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", "What is happening in this audio?", reasoning=True) ``` This sets temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k disabled, seed 0, a 20,480-token completion limit, and a 16,384-token reasoning budget with a 1,024-token allowance to finish reasoning. Use the task instructions documented under [Evaluation Prompts](#evaluation-prompts) as `prompt` and `system_prompt`. #### Word Timestamps and Speaker Diarization The checkpoint bundles the CTC heads used to align the generated transcript to the audio. With `--middleware` set as in the server command above (MTP8 or no speculative decoding), request timestamps with `timestamps=True`, together with a speaker-tagged transcription prompt: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. " "Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. " "Write numbers in their standard written form. " "Put speaker tags on the transcription." ), timestamps=True) alignment = response.model_dump()["ctc_timestamps"] if alignment["error"] is not None: raise RuntimeError(alignment["error"]) for word in alignment["words"]: print(word["word"], word["start"], word["end"], word["speaker"]) ``` The response contains a top-level `ctc_timestamps` object: - `words`: word text, start and end times in seconds relative to the input audio, and the transcript's speaker tag. - `diarization`: speaker activity segments derived from the audio. - `speaker_tag_to_diarization_speaker`: the mapping between transcript tags and diarization speakers. - `error`: `null` on success, or an alignment failure reason. Check this field before using the timestamps. Timestamp requests accept one audio recording, `stream=false`, and `n=1`. Keep `skip_special_tokens=false` and ask for speaker tags when speaker attribution is needed. A transcript without speaker tags is aligned as a single speaker. # Model Overview ### Description NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe is an offline speech and audio model that processes recordings, together with text instructions and optional context, into text responses. NVIDIA developed this [Speech-Augmented Language Model (SALM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09424) for multilingual transcription, speech translation, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, timestamp prediction, language identification, and audio question answering. The audio understanding mixture and the pretrained base components may also contain web-derived data. ### Internally Generated Data, Including Prompt-Collected Data NVIDIA-generated or NVIDIA-transformed training artifacts include: - Granary v2 pseudo-transcriptions and model-generated translations, together with human-improved and Riva-labeled variants - Prompt-controlled Granary v2 task expansions for transcription, contextual transcription, speech QA, inverse text normalization, disfluency-reduced transcription, captioning, and code-switched transcription - Fine-, coarse-, distractor-, partial-, and negative-context variants for contextual ASR - Long-form transcription data and transcript-plus-QA, timestamp, speaker-tag, and translation variants - Multi-speaker task formatting and constructed audio mixtures - Non-speech vocalization and speaking-style annotations - Balanced language-identification prompts and targets - PII tagging and redaction examples - No-speech abstention prompts and empty-response targets - Curated Nemotron text SFT data, audio-instruction, audio-reasoning, and safety-tuning blends Training prompts are developer-authored or generated task instructions associated with prepared training examples. User interactions with a deployed product or model were not used to train the model. ### Self-Sourced Synthetic Data Synthetic and model-generated training data include: - **Nemotron-PII text data:** fully synthetic text examples covering more than 55 PII/PHI categories, with tagged and redacted outputs - **PII-aware ASR data:** synthetic multilingual PII-positive speech examples - **Constructed multi-speaker mixtures:** AuMix examples combining source recordings into conversations of up to eight speakers, including long-form mixtures - **Granary v2 task variants:** generated contextual terms and distractors, speech questions and answers, captions, code-switched targets, and transcript-plus-QA/translation variants - **Audio understanding synthetic-data-generation subsets:** generated captions, questions, answers, instruction-following targets, and reasoning traces for sound, music, speech, and audio-reasoning tasks - **Prompt augmentation:** deterministic and generated prompt variants for transcription, language identification, PII handling, and no-speech abstention Pseudo-labeled ASR and translation examples retain source audio and use model-generated labels; they should not be described as synthetic audio. Constructed multi-speaker mixtures likewise combine source recordings rather than generating new speaker identities. ### Testing Dataset **Data Collection Method by dataset:** Not Applicable **Labeling Method by dataset:** Not Applicable **Properties:** Not Applicable - Testing uses the public benchmark test sets described under [Evaluation Dataset](#evaluation-dataset); there is no separate held-out testing dataset. ### Evaluation Dataset **Data Collection Method by dataset:** Hybrid: Manually-Collected, Automated **Labeling Method by dataset:** Hybrid: Manually-Labeled, Automatic/Sensors **Properties:** - **Data count:** more than 330,000 test examples from public benchmarks, including approximately 243,000 for English, multilingual, multi-speaker, and contextual transcription; 29,000 for language identification; and 57,000 for audio understanding, voice instruction following, and text-only reasoning. Speech translation, long-form, code-switched, and entity benchmarks are evaluated in addition. - **Modalities:** audio with text instructions, references, and context; text-only for the text reasoning benchmarks. - **Nature of the content:** read speech (LibriSpeech, Multilingual LibriSpeech, FLEURS, Common Voice), parliamentary speech (VoxPopuli), podcasts and online video (GigaSpeech), financial earnings calls (Earnings-22, SPGISpeech), meetings (AMI, NOTSOFAR-1, AISHELL-4, AliMeeting), telephone conversations (CALLHOME), interviews (Mixer 6), noisy and degraded recordings (URGENT 2024), code-switched conversations, spoken questions and instructions (VoiceBench, Spoken-MQA), and speech, sound, and music for audio understanding (MMAU, MMAR, AIR-Bench). - **Linguistic characteristics:** 40 supported languages, with the largest share in English, including Indian-accented English and Hindi (Monsoon), Mandarin meetings, and Hindi–English, Bengali–English, and Mandarin–English code-switching; transcripts are scored both verbatim and in normalized written form, depending on the benchmark. ### Benchmark Results Results are grouped by task. **↓ Lower is better; ↑ higher is better.** Error rates and accuracy are percentages unless another scale is shown. Install both into one environment with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and download the checkpoint: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech.git nemo-speech cd nemo-speech uv venv --python 3.13 .venv UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$PWD/.venv uv sync --extra asr --extra vllm --locked --no-install-project uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e . # PyAV decodes compressed audio formats, such as M4A, without a system FFmpeg. uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps av==19.0.2 # vLLM requires OpenCV, which NeMo's dependency settings exclude. uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93 source .venv/bin/activate hf download nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B --local-dir ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B ``` #### Start the Server Start an OpenAI-compatible server on one GPU, with MTP speculative decoding proposing eight tokens (MTP8): ```bash export VLLM_PLUGINS=nemo_speechlm # Allow vLLM to decode recordings up to one hour long (the default is 600 seconds). export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=3600 export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=180 # Word timestamps require the V1 model runner. export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 vllm serve ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --served-model-name nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \ --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 192 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-async-scheduling \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":{"count":6,"length":120000000}}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}' \ --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 \ --trust-request-mm-kwargs \ --middleware nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm.ctc_serving.ctc_timestamp_middleware ``` The server listens on `127.0.0.1:8000`; use `--host` and `--port` to change this. The settings target an H100 with 80 GB of GPU memory; other hardware or workloads may need a different `--gpu-memory-utilization`, `--max-model-len`, or `--max-num-seqs`. The checkpoint contains two MTP depths implemented with a repeated layer. MTP8 reuses that layer to propose eight tokens; it does not require eight distinct trained MTP layers. The best mode depends on the GPU and the workload. These are rough throughput estimates, excluding server startup, for the English Open ASR and Monsoon datasets with reasoning disabled. Throughput depends on recording length, output length, batch size, and GPU memory settings; it is not a single-request latency estimate. Keep ReplaySSM (`--use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none`) and prefix caching disabled, as in the command above. The first requests after startup are slower while kernels are compiled and warmed up.
DFlash2 draft model As an alternative to MTP, the separate draft model [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2) proposes up to 15 tokens at once with vLLM's `dflash` method. DFlash2 and MTP are alternatives and are not combined. K=7 is the recommended starting point; K=15 was slower on the tested ASR workload. vLLM 0.32.0 needs a small fix to its DFlash2 implementation; without it, the server can fail when requests finish. Apply it once to the environment: ```bash python - <<'EOF_PATCH' from pathlib import Path import vllm path = Path(vllm.__file__).parent / "model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash2.py" source = path.read_text() if "safe_anchor_token_ids" not in source: old = " successors = successor_table[candidate_ids]\n" anchor = " anchor_token_ids[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, top_k)," assert source.count(old) == 1 and source.count(anchor) == 1, "unexpected vLLM version" source = source.replace(old, ( " safe_anchor_token_ids = anchor_token_ids.clamp(\n" " min=0, max=predecessor_table.shape[0] - 1\n" " )\n" + old )).replace(anchor, " safe_anchor_token_ids[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, top_k),") path.write_text(source) EOF_PATCH ``` The fix modifies vLLM source code (Copyright contributors to the vLLM project), which is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, not under OpenMDW-1.1; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Then start the server with the following options instead of `--speculative-config` and `--middleware` from the command above. Word timestamps are not available with DFlash2, so the CTC alignment is disabled: ```bash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7,"model":"nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2"}' \ --hf-overrides '{"ctc_timestamps":{"enabled":false}}' ``` vLLM runs DFlash2 only on its V2 model runner, so also run `unset VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` before starting the server.
#### Send a Request Send audio to the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with an OpenAI-compatible client. The following function covers transcription, reasoning, and word timestamps: ```python import base64 from pathlib import Path from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") def ask(audio_path, prompt, system_prompt="", reasoning=False, timestamps=False): audio = base64.b64encode(Path(audio_path).read_bytes()).decode() messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}] if system_prompt else [] messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio_url", "audio_url": {"url": f"data:audio/wav;base64,{audio}"}}, ]}) extra_body = { "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": reasoning}, "skip_special_tokens": False, # keep speaker and event tags "spaces_between_special_tokens": False, "seed": 0, } if reasoning: extra_body.update(top_k=-1, thinking_token_budget=17408) extra_body["chat_template_kwargs"]["reasoning_budget"] = 16384 if timestamps: extra_body["mm_processor_kwargs"] = {"capture_ctc_timestamps": True} return client.chat.completions.create( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B", messages=messages, temperature=0.6 if reasoning else 0, top_p=0.95 if reasoning else 1.0, max_tokens=20480 if reasoning else 16384, extra_body=extra_body, ) response = ask("audio.wav", "Transcribe the following audio.") print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` A dense one-hour conversation can need about 20,000 output tokens. For long recordings, raise `max_tokens` or remove it, so that the transcript is not truncated. Transcription uses temperature 0 with reasoning disabled. For audio understanding, enable reasoning and ask a question about the audio: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", "What is happening in this audio?", reasoning=True) ``` This sets temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k disabled, seed 0, a 20,480-token completion limit, and a 16,384-token reasoning budget with a 1,024-token allowance to finish reasoning. Use the task instructions documented under [Evaluation Prompts](#evaluation-prompts) as `prompt` and `system_prompt`. #### Word Timestamps and Speaker Diarization The checkpoint bundles the CTC heads used to align the generated transcript to the audio. With `--middleware` set as in the server command above, request timestamps with `timestamps=True`, together with a speaker-tagged transcription prompt: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. " "Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. " "Write numbers in their standard written form. " "Put speaker tags on the transcription." ), timestamps=True) alignment = response.model_dump()["ctc_timestamps"] if alignment["error"] is not None: raise RuntimeError(alignment["error"]) for word in alignment["words"]: print(word["word"], word["start"], word["end"], word["speaker"]) ``` The response contains a top-level `ctc_timestamps` object: - `words`: word text, start and end times in seconds relative to the input audio, and the transcript's speaker tag. - `diarization`: speaker activity segments derived from the audio. - `speaker_tag_to_diarization_speaker`: the mapping between transcript tags and diarization speakers. - `error`: `null` on success, or an alignment failure reason. Check this field before using the timestamps. Timestamp requests accept one audio recording, `stream=false`, and `n=1`. Keep `skip_special_tokens=false` and ask for speaker tags when speaker attribution is needed. A transcript without speaker tags is aligned as a single speaker. Use the `diarization` segments, rather than word timestamps, when evaluating diarization. ### SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni) serves this model for whole-file transcription on `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, on one GPU, from the BF16 or FP8 checkpoint (both validated on one H100 80 GB and one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). It does not need NeMo. After [installing SGLang-Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/get_started/installation.md) 0.2.0, which pins SGLang 0.5.22: ```bash sgl-omni serve \ --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --model-name nemotron-transcribe \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --port 8000 curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F model=nemotron-transcribe \ -F file=@audio.wav ``` Word timestamps, speaker-attributed output, translation and speculative decoding are not part of this integration. See the [SGLang-Omni Nemotron Transcribe cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/nemotron_transcribe.html) for its settings, streaming and a tuned profile for short clips. ### Transformers usage 🤗 Install 🤗 Transformers from source: ```sh pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers ```
Transcription ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B" samples = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") audio = [samples + "en-Alice_woman.wav", samples + "diarization_example.mp3"] speaker_attributed_prompt = ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) prompt = [None, speaker_attributed_prompt] inputs = processor.apply_transcription_request(audio, prompt=prompt).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024) texts = processor.decode(outputs[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) print([text.replace(processor.tokenizer.pad_token, "") for text in texts]) ```
Speaker-attributed transcription ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B" samples = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") prompt = ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) conversation = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio", "path": samples + "diarization_example.mp3"}, ], } ] inputs = processor.apply_chat_template( conversation, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=True, enable_thinking=False, ).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024) text = processor.decode(outputs[0, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) print(text) ``` `processor.extract_speaker_dict` splits the output into one dictionary per speaker turn: ```python for turn in processor.extract_speaker_dict(text): print(turn) ```
Word timestamps and speaker diarization Requires `torchaudio` and `scipy`. ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B" samples = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") prompt = ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) inputs = processor.apply_transcription_request(samples + "diarization_example.mp3", prompt=prompt).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, return_word_timestamp_logits=True) texts = processor.decode(outputs.sequences[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) timestamps = processor.align_word_timestamps( texts, outputs.word_timestamp_logits, inputs.input_features_mask, outputs.speaker_logits, ) print(timestamps[0]["chunks"][:3]) ```
See the [Transformers documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/nemotron3_5_transcribe) for more. ### Evaluation Prompts Use these shortened task-specific templates as starting points. For ASR evaluation, use [Exact ASR Benchmark Prompts](#exact-asr-benchmark-prompts). The ASR benchmark environment uses vLLM 0.28.0 and NeMo Speech with the FP32 preservation change from [PR #16357](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech/pull/16357), which is included in the main branch, with MTP2. For audio understanding, spoken instructions, and text reasoning, use [Exact Understanding and Reasoning Prompts](#exact-understanding-and-reasoning-prompts), which lists the complete evaluated system prompts; keep the prepared user questions and choices unchanged. For the remaining benchmark families, use [All Evaluated Prompts](#all-evaluated-prompts), which contains the complete evaluated prompts and reasoning flags. Replace placeholders with the actual languages, labels, or context. #### Prompt Recommendations For these tasks, keep the **system prompt empty**. Send the instruction in the **user message**, alongside the audio. | Task | Recommended user prompt | Why we suggest it | | --- | --- | --- | | Verbatim ASR, including multilingual and long-form audio | `Audio transcription. Language: as spoken. Wording: verbatim, including fillers and repetitions. Formatting: punctuation and capitalization. Output: transcript only.` | Preserves wording and language with an explicit output format. | | Clean written transcript | Replace the wording clause above with `omit fillers and accidental repetitions; keep the remaining spoken wording unchanged`. Add `numbers in their standard written form` if needed. | Makes cleanup and number normalization explicit. | | Speaker attribution / word timestamps | `Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription.` | Provides stable speaker tags for attribution and timestamp alignment; also enable timestamp capture. | | Near-field speaker only (experimental) | `Transcribe this audio. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write numbers as spoken. No punctuation or capitalization. Transcribe only the speaker nearest to the microphone. Do not transcribe any other voices.` | Ignores background voices, such as far-field speech in a meeting room. With LibriSpeech test-clean speech mixed with far-field NOTSOFAR-1 audio, the WER is 4.78% with this prompt and 27.32% with a single-speaker transcription prompt. | | Code-switching / script control | `Transcribe verbatim in the original languages. Preserve hesitations and false starts. Write in

# TextPro-SLM-3B-Global

**Your speech LLM can be a prosody-aware text LLM.**

**Built with Qwen.**

TextPro-SLM brings speech closer to a text LLM's native input format: transcript tokens carry linguistic content, and compact prosody embeddings carry complementary acoustic information. The paper studies how this input-side factorization preserves semantic capabilities while learning paralinguistic understanding with roughly **1,000 hours of LLM training audio**.

[Paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Jsjmo8eX29) · [GitHub project](https://github.com/dreamtheater123/TextPro-SLM) · [Paired WhisperPro](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/WhisperPro)

## Checkpoint

This is the original **3B global-prepending** stage-2 checkpoint (step 1272), paired with the original WhisperPro. It accepts speech clips of at most **30 seconds**. The separate 30Plus models provide a segmentation-based long-audio extension.

| Component | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Text backbone | Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, fully fine-tuned |
| Speech encoder | WhisperPro, decoder-layer-16 prosody features |
| Projector | 1280 → 2048 → 2048, GELU, BF16 |
| Fusion | Global prepending |
| Audio | Mono, 16 kHz, at most 30 seconds |
| LLM context | 32,768 tokens |
| Output | Text response |

A single global prosody vector is prepended to transcript tokens.

The trained prosody marker is `<|repo_name|>` (ID 151663). Preserve the supplied tokenizer and the fusion settings in `textpro_config.json`.

## Download

```bash
pip install "huggingface-hub>=0.36,<1"
hf download qqjz/TextPro-SLM-3B-Global --local-dir TextPro-SLM-3B-Global
```

This Hub repository contains **weights, configurations, tokenizer artifacts, and documentation only**. Inference code, dependencies, and usage examples are being prepared separately in the [GitHub project](https://github.com/dreamtheater123/TextPro-SLM). Loading the text backbone alone does not perform prosody-aware speech inference.

## Files and verification

`llm/` contains the complete fine-tuned language model and tokenizer. `projector.safetensors` contains the compact trained projector. `textpro_config.json` records fusion settings and pins the original WhisperPro revision. `SHA256SUMS.json` records artifact sizes and hashes.

The four projector parameter tensors are unchanged from the original checkpoint. The export was checked locally and on GPU: parameter hashes, synthetic-input projections, injected embeddings, next-token logits, and fixed-seed generated tokens matched the original implementation on two real-audio checks. An obsolete total-size statistic in the shard index was corrected; all tensor payloads and parameter-to-shard mappings are unchanged. Original-index and corrected-index model loading were both checked.

These are artifact-equivalence checks, not new benchmark measurements. Evaluation results and experimental settings are described in the paper.

## Model family

| Encoder | Speech LLM | Fusion / audio handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [WhisperPro](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/WhisperPro) | [TextPro-SLM-7B-Global](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/TextPro-SLM-7B-Global) | Global prepending, original ≤30s |
| [WhisperPro](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/WhisperPro) | [TextPro-SLM-7B-Interleaving](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/TextPro-SLM-7B-Interleaving) | 5:1 interleaving, original ≤30s |
| [WhisperPro](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/WhisperPro) | [TextPro-SLM-3B-Global](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/TextPro-SLM-3B-Global) | Global prepending, original ≤30s |
| [WhisperPro-30Plus](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/WhisperPro-30Plus) | [TextPro-SLM-7B-30Plus](https://huggingface.co/qqjz/TextPro-SLM-7B-30Plus) | Global prepending, segmented long audio |

## Limitations

Transcription errors can propagate to the answer. Performance can vary with language, recording conditions, speaker characteristics, and domain. Prosody pooling compresses temporal detail, and generated answers may contain hallucinations. This release returns text rather than synthesized speech. The 30Plus checkpoints are separate artifacts; this model card does not claim unlimited audio duration or new benchmark accuracy.

## License and provenance

**Built with Qwen.** This checkpoint inherits the **Qwen Research License** from its Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct backbone. The upstream grant covers non-commercial research/evaluation; commercial use requires a separate license from Alibaba Cloud. See `LICENSE` and `Notice`.

The paired WhisperPro derives from OpenAI Whisper large-v3 and has its own Apache-2.0 license. See `MODIFICATIONS.md` for the modified artifact list and export changes.

# Maya 2 Native **Open speech. Native voices.** Streaming text-to-speech for **11 Indian languages and English**. **12 languages · 20 voices · Voice cloning · Apache-2.0** [Listen](#listen-in-12-languages) · [Get started](#quickstart) · [Explore voices](#voices) · [Benchmarks](#voicearena-benchmark) · [Evaluation](#evaluation) · [Code](https://github.com/MayaResearch/maya2-native)
Maya 2 Native brings streaming speech generation to the languages people use every day. Built by **Maya Research**, it generates **24 kHz speech** in 12 languages, with **20 built-in voices** and **zero-shot voice cloning from 3–10 seconds of reference audio**.
